metas.note: one dot on the back of the car on the right on this section of the 3 in Santa Cruz
metas.footer: Credit to: All Major Santa Cruz Dusts by Jupa

metas.name: 251 road lines - 251 road lines
metas.note: The 251 has these Danish style roadlines. quite possibly the only non divided road in Arge with these roadlines. Also the northern part of the road has glitchy sunset coverage
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: 3 smudge+dirt - RP29 3 Smudges + Dirt
metas.note: The RP29 in Santa Cruz has 3 smudges on the camera and is a dirt road. The RN40 also has these smudges but it is paved.
metas.footer: Credit to The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: 3 smudge+paved - RN40 3 Smudges Paved
metas.note: The RN40 (Bajo Caracoles <-> Perito Moreno) in Santa Cruz has 3 smudges on the camera. This is also seen on the RP29, but that road is dirt
metas.footer: Credit to The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: B type no top - B Type No Top
metas.note:
This is what I call a B type pole, featuring a lower bar with 2 insulator racks facing downwards and a one-sided bar above it with more down-facing insulators.

This is a variant of the B type pole where the vertical bar ends at the top horizontal bar unlike the standard version where it extends past it. Notably, (almost) every B Type pole in Buenos Aires Province will be of this variant. So if the vertical bar extends past the top horizontal bar, you will not be in BA. This is extremely helpful for regionguessing the central part of the country. Keep in mind that it can be found anywhere however, but by far the biggest cluster is in BA.
metas.footer: Credit: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: B type short cap - B Type Variant - Short Cap
metas.note:
This is what I call a B type pole, featuring a lower bar with 2 insulator racks facing downwards and a one-sided bar above it with more down-facing insulators.

In this variant, there is a short cap immediately after the top horizontal beam. I have only ever seen this variant in Cordoba and La Rioja (credit to BCosign for spotting it in La Rioja, I had only seen it in Cordoba).
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: B type standard top length - B Type Variant - Standard Length Top
metas.note:
This is what I call a B type pole, featuring a lower bar with 2 insulator racks facing downwards and a one-sided bar above it with more down-facing insulators.

In this variant, the vertical beam extends above the top horizontal bar at roughly about the same length between the two horizontal bars. This variant is most often found in Entre Rios and Santiago Del Estero and sometimes in Tucuman, Catamarca, and San Luis.
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: beech forests - Beech Forests
metas.note: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Butia yatay palm - Butia Yatay Palm
metas.note: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: C type no cap - C Type No Cap
metas.note:
This is what I call a C Type Pole, where there are 3 alternating horizontal beams with down-facing insulators on the end of each of them. They are found everywhere with the exceptions of La Pampa (although a little Cordoba spill) and Misiones. More importantly, there are several region-specific variants.

This is probably the most useful variant, where there is no cap (but it still extends above). They can rarely be found scattered randomly, but are by far the most common in Cordoba Province and 2nd most common in BA (but still a lot more common in Cordoba).
metas.footer: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: C type wide cap - C Type Variant - Wide Cap
metas.note:
This is what I call a C Type Pole, where there are 3 alternating horizontal beams with down-facing insulators on the end of each of them. They are found everywhere with the exceptions of La Pampa (although a little Cordoba spill) and Misiones. More importantly, there are several region-specific variants.

This is where there is a wide cap going both directions. It is most common in San Luis but can also be found more rarely in Cordoba.
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: calden - Caldén
metas.note:
Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

NOTE: This tree can sometimes be confused with other trees such as the White Carob.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Caranday palm - Caranday Palm
metas.note: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Caranday wax palm - Caranday wax palm
metas.note: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: cardon - Cardón
metas.note: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: center shape dust - center shape dust
metas.note: weird center smudge on the dust on the back of the car in chubut
metas.footer: Credit to: All Major Chubut Smudges by Jupa

metas.name: Comdoro Rivadavia -  Comodoro Rivadavia
metas.note: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: cordoba km marker - Cordoba KM Marker
metas.note: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: cordoba mts - Cordoba Western Mountains
metas.note:
These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.

NOTE: They are not as high as the mountains in the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Cordoba sticker - Cordoba Sticker
metas.note:
Cordoba province has a very consistent back-of-sign sticker that appears as a red circle. It’s most commonly on the back of stop signs but appears on all sorts of other signs too like yield signs and even directional signs.

It seems to be relatively new (Gen 4 coverage has it, but 2013 Gen 3 doesn’t
metas.footer: Credit to Mac Hays

metas.name: corn - Corn
metas.note: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in Córdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Double V dust - Double V dust
metas.note: Double V looking dust on the back of the car
metas.footer: Credit to: All Major Santa Cruz Dusts by Jupa

metas.name: flat barren landscape - Flat Barren Landscape
metas.note: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: flat barren red soil - flat barren red soil
metas.note: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: flat grass+ no bushes - flat grass+ no bushes
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: gen 4 volcanic rocs - gen 4 volcanic rocks
metas.note: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Grassland - Grassland
metas.note: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: IOMF poletop Corrientes - IOMF poletop Corrientes
metas.note: "Isle Of Man Flag" style poletop. Corrientes Variant (vertical bar barely goes above the top, if at all)
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: IOMF poletop Jujuy - IOMF poletop Jujuy
metas.note: "Isle Of Man Flag" style poletop. Jujuy + Misiones Variant (vertical bar goes far above the top)
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: IOMF poletop Misiones - IOMF poletop Misiones
metas.note: "Isle Of Man Flag" style poletop. Jujuy + Misiones Variant (vertical bar goes far above the top)
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: IOMF poletop San Luis - IOMF poletop San Luis
metas.note: "Isle Of Man Flag" style poletop. San Luis Variant (vertical bar goes a bit above the top)
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: la pampa t junction - La Pampa T-Junction
metas.note: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: latvian poles - Latvian Poles
metas.note: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza. (mendoza is kinda fake its basically only La Rioja)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: left 3 stripes dust - left 3 stripes dust
metas.note: 3 stripes on the left back of the car. Might be found on some other roads in this general area of East Chubut but from what I see most of it is now Gen 4.
metas.footer: Credit to: All Major Chubut Smudges by Jupa

metas.name: macaw palm - Macaw Palm
metas.note: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: mar del plata architecture - Mar Del Plata Architecture
metas.note: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: mendoza single insulator - mendoza single insulator
metas.note: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: mendoza vinyards - Mendoza Vineyards
metas.note:
If you see vineyards with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.

NOTE: There are multiple wine regions in Argentina, but the Mendoza wine region is the most recognisable one of them all.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: monkey puzzle - Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.note:
The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.

NOTE: They are seen on the other side in Chile as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Pampas grass - Pampas Grass
metas.note: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: pink trumpet tree - Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.note: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal and General Mosconi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: red brick - Red Brick
metas.note: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: red rock formations - Red Rock Formations+Dam
metas.note:
Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

NOTE: Sometimes you will be able to see this dam in the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Red soil - Red Soil
metas.note:
Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

NOTE: Brazil and Argentina can look similar in this region. Make sure to look for other clues first.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: redish road+needlegrass - reddish road+needle-grass
metas.note: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: rio colorado sunrise - rio colorado sunrise
metas.note: Sunrise coverage with bad image quality and multiple blurs is found on a short part of the RN251 and RN22, west of Río Colorado. (the 22 might be overwritten w/ new coverage)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: RN16 - RN16 Danish Roadlines
metas.note: The RN16 has danish style Roadlines. There are a handful of roads that have this in Arge. What makes this one unique is it is divided, and the inner line is yellow. The RN16 also meets this criteria, so use the road angle to determine which is which.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: rn40 sunrise - RN40 Sunrise
metas.note:
Sunrise coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with Neuquén.

NOTE: The quality of the coverage improves closer to the border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: rn65 - RN65 "death road"
metas.note:
The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this small, dangerous road in the clouds.

NOTE: This road can look similar to the “Road of Death” in Bolivia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: rn68 red hills - RN68 Red Hills
metas.note: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: RN7 - RN7 Danish Roadliens
metas.note: The RN 7 has Danish syle roadlines. There are a handful of roads with Danish Roadlines. What makes this one unique is it is divided, and the inner line is yellow. The only other road that meets this criteria is the R16, but they look different and you can use the road angle to determine which is which.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: RN9 Rosario  - RN9 Rosario-BA Danish Roadlines
metas.note: The RN9 from Rosario to (roughly) Buenos Aires has danish style outer lines. What makes this one unique is it is divided, and both the outer and inner line are white.
metas.footer: ty to Melting Ice

metas.name: rp25 snow coverage - RP25 Snow Coverage
metas.note: This snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: rp293 - RN293
metas.note: Melting snow coverage is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: salt pans - Salt Pans
metas.note:
Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

NOTE: They can also be found in southwestern Bolivia and northeastern Chile, but without Generation 4 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Sandy soil + vegetation - Sandy soil + vegetation
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: sawdust car - Sawdust Car
metas.note: The “sawdust” car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: semi coastal grassy hills - semi coastal grassy hills
metas.note: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: small lakes - Small Lakes
metas.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: sorghum - Sorghum
metas.note: Fields of sorghum can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, Córdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: sugarcane - Sugarcane plantations
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are most common in Tucumán, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: sunflower fields - Sunflower Fields
metas.note: Fields of sunflowers are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Thick Slanted Stripes dust - Thick Slanted Stripes dust
metas.note: Thick Slanted Stripes smudged into the back of the car in Santa Cruz
metas.footer: Credit to: All Major Santa Cruz Dusts by Jupa

metas.name: toothpick cactus - Toothpick Cactus
metas.note: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: tree plantations - Tree Plantations
metas.note:
The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

NOTE: Uruguay and southern Brazil have them as well. Make sure to look at other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Tucuman pole sticker - Tucuman pole stickers
metas.note: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in Tucumán.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: upside down trident pole - upside down trident pole
metas.note: This upside-down trident pole with a diagonal extension is unique to Misiones Province.
metas.footer: Credit to: Complete Guide to Argentina Poletops by Kyleb.b

metas.name: ushuaia - Ushuaia
metas.note:
These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

NOTE: Ushuaia is the southernmost city of Argentina and the province capital of Tierra del Fuego.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Valdes Peninsula - Valdes Peninsula
metas.note: Unusually wide dirt roads and flat geography make the Valdes peninsula of Eastern Chubut recognizable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Western mountains - Far West Mountains
metas.note:
Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

NOTE: It is rare to find mountains in eastern Argentina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: wild sunflowers - Wild Sunflower
metas.note: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
